doc.title: Reggie Watkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, May 22, 2018

title: Taking risks in improvisation
summary: Watkins says mistakes were never an issue thanks to his junior high grounding in basic scales and blues.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: Were you more inclined to take risks than other musicians in the band as far as improvisation? I guess what I mean by that, a lot of students are really afraid of mistakes or what they perceive as mistakes. And when they hit one it’s like they stop and make a face or whatever. I wonder if that was not an issue for you.

That wasn’t an issue for me. And again, I had that background in junior high of having the chance to get an introduction to improvisation and a B flat blues scale, etcetera. So I always enjoyed those broad concepts of A major scale, a B flat, a blues scale, four-four time, like that to me was enough comfort to say oh just go ahead and play you know. And then you learn things as you go along just larger concepts in music.
